task.title: Write a campaign results email to a bakery client
task.brief: You ran a two-week Diwali campaign for a bakery in Hyderabad. The results are in the material below. Write an email to the owner, Ms. Farah, in 15 to 20 minutes. A good email: gives a short summary first, explains in plain words what worked and what did not (use the numbers), and gives 3 clear, practical suggestions for the next campaign. Keep it under 250 words. No jargon without a short explanation.
task.material:
Campaign: Diwali sweet boxes, 20 Oct to 3 Nov. Total budget ₹60,000.

Channel | Spend | Clicks | Orders | Revenue
Instagram ads | ₹30,000 | 6,000 | 45 | ₹54,000
Google Search ads | ₹20,000 | 1,600 | 70 | ₹1,05,000
WhatsApp broadcast (opted-in, 2,000 customers) | ₹2,000 | 500 | 60 | ₹84,000
Influencer post (1 food blogger) | ₹8,000 | 900 | 5 | ₹6,000

Notes: Instagram cost per click was low, but many visitors left the order page. 30 orders were lost because the website showed 'out of stock' for kaju katli boxes on 30 Oct. Average order value is about ₹1,200 to ₹1,500.
key_points: Opens with a clear one or two line summary of overall results (about ₹2.49 lakh revenue on ₹60,000 spend)
Names WhatsApp and Google Search as the best channels, using ROAS or cost per order
Points out the influencer post gave poor return (₹8,000 spent, ₹6,000 revenue)
Notes Instagram brought cheap clicks but few orders, suggesting an order page or offer problem
Mentions the stock-out loss and suggests stock checks or alerts
Gives 3 specific, practical suggestions, such as moving budget to Search and WhatsApp
Polite, plain-language tone suited to a small business owner

rubric.label: Correct reading of numbers
rubric.guide: 0 = numbers wrong or ignored, 3 = mostly right with small slips, 5 = all key figures read and compared correctly

rubric.label: Useful suggestions
rubric.guide: 0 = no suggestions or vague ones, 3 = sensible but generic, 5 = three specific steps that follow from the data

rubric.label: Clarity and structure
rubric.guide: 0 = confusing or rambling, 3 = understandable but loose, 5 = summary first, short paragraphs, easy for the owner to act on

rubric.label: Tone
rubric.guide: 0 = rude, pushy or full of jargon, 3 = polite but stiff, 5 = warm, professional and plain
